references.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: cinematic DCC software operation illustration for a DCC-MCP explainer advert.
Input image 1 is a real Blender manual screenshot used ONLY as a layout and UI identity reference. Reconstruct a clean, believable Blender desktop interface in neutral charcoal dark theme. REMOVE all translucent green, purple and red explanatory tint from the manual screenshot. Keep recognizable Blender top menu/workspace tabs, left viewport toolbar, right Outliner and Properties, small bottom timeline. Front-on flat screen capture style, absolutely no monitor device, room, people, hands, perspective distortion or surrounding border. Landscape 16:9 at highest practical resolution.
Main viewport: a stunning photoreal rendered preview of one original unbranded over-ear headphone design, oversized rounded rectangular ear cups in fine bead-blasted silver aluminum, deep midnight-blue fabric ear cushions, smooth arched metal headband with dark-blue padding. Elegant professional industrial design. Headphones standing three-quarter view on a charcoal studio plinth, softbox lighting with tasteful cool-blue rim reflection, crisp real metal microtexture. Whole headphone silhouette visible and large inside the main viewport. The model occupies x~0.28–0.66 y~0.18–0.79 of full canvas. Studio background nearly black, dramatic but realistic product photography look. Clearly a rendered product in software, not abstract toy art.
The viewport should occupy about left 80 percent of the image, with realistic thin toolbars. Right Outliner can have short accurate item labels only: Headphones, Camera, Key, Fill, Rim. Right Properties shows Materials with restrained actual-looking controls. Correct normal Blender labels, not invented AI control panels. No chat overlays, no marketing text, no logo except normal Blender application icon, no success logs, no benchmarks, no fake progress indicators, no watermark. This is an AI-reconstructed operation illustration, not an execution screenshot; disclosure will be added in the final video.
Create ONE polished final-after state frame, composition suitable for a before/after match cut. This establishes the exact headphone identity and fixed camera for later states.
